translated: My 7‑year‑old daughter was scratched on her lower lip by our dog. It bled for a moment and then stopped. The next day the lip looked normal, but it was a little swollen, like it would be after a minor cut. Now her throat is sore and her tonsils are swollen. Could this be from the scratch? On the inside of the lip where the dog scratched, there is a small canker sore. It’s not large, and I have applied Chloryseptic to it and the surrounding area. Doctor, please look at her current condition. She was scratched on Tuesday and today is Thursday, when these additional issues appeared. I’m just a bit confused about whether I’m overthinking this.

Hi! My 2‑year‑old son has had terrible diarrhea for more than a week. We took him to the doctor, and after the examination they said he has a bad strep infection. He was given Moxypen for 7 days. Yesterday we went back to the doctor to check his throat to confirm that the infection is cleared. The doctor said my son's tonsils are very swollen and filled with blood vessels. Please, doctor, look at his current condition. They prescribed azithromycin for 3 days. What does that mean? Does my son need to take so many antibiotics?

My 5‑year‑old son has a platelet count of 166. He has had a fever with mild stomach ache. The doctor gave him Amoxil Forte because his tonsils are swollen and red. Please, doctor, look at his current condition. Is it safe for him to take amoxicillin since we are monitoring his platelet count?

Hi, I have had small spots on my tonsils for a long time and I have a very bad bad breath. Sometimes I feel burning in my throat and hands, and I also get headaches. In the mornings I have no appetite, and when I try to eat, I feel nauseous all day. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. Suddenly I feel heat on my face and also feel cold. I am very worried; I just want to know what is happening to me. My weight is 57 kg and I am 19 years old. Thank you, sorry for the bad English.

Can wisdom teeth affect your tonsils? My tonsils have been swollen for the past three days, feeling very similar to a strep throat, but I have no other symptoms like fever or weakness. I have four wisdom teeth, three of which are impacted, and this happens 4–5 times a year. Please, doctor, evaluate my current condition.

My 7-year-old son has a headache, sore body, throat pain, and his eyes are glassy. Please, doctor, look at his eyes. He fell quite hard yesterday. His appetite is poor. His eyes look sunken or swollen. Is this due to the fall or just a minor infection?

My daughter is 9 years old. She has a history of three nut allergies. After dinner she took a shower and her eyes became swollen. Please, doctor, look at these eyes below. She says there is itching, only here, not in the throat or anywhere else. I examined her body and there are no hives. I gave her Benadryl, just to be safe. Should I take her to the emergency room?

My little daughter, who is 7 years old, fell and hit her head on a doll's house. She has a headache and her eyelid is bruised and swollen. Please, doctor, look at her eyes. She had an ice pack on for 20 minutes and it is still swollen, but she has now fallen asleep. Should I be concerned? Thank you.

My 9‑month‑old son fell from the bed onto a marble floor and his eye swelled up immediately. Please have the doctor examine his eye. It turned black. Now the swelling and marks are fine, but his eye is smaller than the other one and it gets a little swollen when he lifts it. It's been three weeks and I'm very worried.

My 13‑month‑old daughter developed two bumps in the middle of her nose two days ago, and a bump under one eye that became quite swollen. Please, doctor, look at her eyes. She is now rubbing them, and the swelling has spread to the right eye, leaving her with two swollen eyes and a slightly reddened bump beneath them.

My child is just one year old, and he fell ill a few days ago. On the first day he was coughing, and this morning he woke up with some eye problems, then his nose got blocked again, he is having difficulty breathing, and he is wheezing. Please, doctor, examine his eyes. Kindly tell me what is happening.

My six-year-old son has swelling around his nose and eyes. He has been having headaches for the past few days. Please, doctor, look at his eyes, they are down and behind. His nose is slightly running. He is very upset. Is this more likely a sinus infection or could he have put something in his nose? What should I do?

Hello, my 3-year-old daughter (30 lb) swallowed one 25 ml carprofen tablet and since last night she has been complaining about eye discomfort; her eyes are slightly red and she is rubbing them, which has never happened before. I gave her a thorough wash from head to toe in the shower and rinsed her eyes well, and she seems a bit better, though there is some swelling under her eyes. Please, doctor, look at the eyes shown here. I don’t know if this is caused by the tablet or if she got something on her hands (I can’t tell) and rubbed her eyes. I previously called the poison control center and they said she might just have some irritation and that’s all. What is your opinion?

I have a 2‑month‑old baby. Small red spots have developed on his face, for which I am using Diprobase cream because his skin is very dry. Later, larger pustule‑like spots also appeared around his neck. The doctor said it could be due to a fungal infection causing the skin to break down. He prescribed clotrimazole cream to apply three times a day. Now the pustules look better, but they have turned into white patches, which worries me because they look like vitiligo and may never fade. Please, doctor, review the current condition below. Help me and tell me what these patches are and whether they will fade. Thank you.

My 20‑month‑old child has red spots all over the body and face, especially swelling around the eyes on the face. I think it itches because he rubs it hard on his stomach and then cries! He had a severe bout of chickenpox a year ago, and today’s rash is not that type; it’s covering his body like a sheet and turning it completely red! He also has a fever, but his hands and feet are normal. Please see the current condition below. Cold! The doctor didn’t mention any allergy and wants to see him again after a few days, but I’m worried! Any suggestions would be appreciated. Thank you.

My 4-year-old daughter has a small patch on one hand and on the back of her neck. It is slightly red and bumpy with a tiny black‑center appearance. Please assess this condition. It was not there in the morning but appeared by night. She has no fever and the rash is not itching.

My 4-year-old child has had a rash all over the body and a high fever for a few days. We went to the doctor, and they said this rash is not part of the eczema my daughter presented with two years ago. All the tests came back negative, so now I don’t know what to think. The doctor said my son’s rash is due to the fever, but the rash appeared before the fever... I need help. Please see the current condition described below.

We have a 16‑month‑old baby who has had a serious allergy for the past three to four months. The skin becomes red in the form of a rash. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. The baby has a lot of itching and is uncomfortable while sleeping. The sleep does not seem sound. Could you suggest what we should do now? It is mentioned here that I, the baby's father, have had acute allergies since I was 23 years old.

My 8‑month‑old daughter had a temperature of 39.1 °C a few days ago. We took her to our doctor, who diagnosed a virus. Her temperature is now normal, but she has red spots/rash all over her body. When she lies on one side for a while, the rash is more noticeable on her face. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. I can’t tell whether the rash is part of the virus or a reaction to paracetamol. Any suggestions would be appreciated.

My child is 2 years and 4 months old and has some discomfort in the skin on the right arm side. The pediatrician said it is some kind of viral infection and, if needed, to apply Caladryl and give Atarax syrup when the itching is severe. How long will the treatment take? Please, doctor, see the current condition described below. It hasn't cleared yet; it has been three days and it is still on the same side.

My 21‑month‑old child's skin develops a red, raised rash, which seems to occur after eating cinnamon toast, but we think it could also be caused by sugar‑free syrup. It has also happened with sugar‑free jelly. Is there a way to give sugar‑free products so they don’t harm him? Please, doctor, look at his current condition. If his skin gets a rash, what internal harm could it be causing? Thank you!

My 14‑month‑old child has a rash on his hands and cheeks. Please, doctor, look at the current condition below. They appear as small raised white or skin‑colored dots. I see him scratching his hands but not his face. His cheeks are just red. Could this be worms? Does he need deworming, or could it be something else?

My baby has very severe skin discoloration from diaper rash and medication that was prescribed for his foot. He is half white and half Indian, so he has a slightly tanned skin color. Will this ever get better? Will the skin on his bottom ever become tan like the rest of his body? Please, doctor, look at his current condition. Kindly give advice. Thank you.

My 13-year-old son has been having the same illness continuously for the past two or three years... sore throat and tonsils, achy legs, low-grade fever, and he always vomits up mucus. This happens every couple of months, and he often complains of a sore throat and his tonsils seem to be quite swollen. Please, doctor, look at his current condition. He snores fiercely and breathes through his mouth when he sleeps. We just went on vacation and no one could sleep because he was snoring so loudly. He had this infection two weeks ago when we were away, and this morning he started it again and vomited up mucus five times today. Should he see an ear, throat, and nose specialist? I have taken him to a doctor several times without any results.

My grandson is two and a half years old, and he suddenly started scratching his skin and feels uncomfortable while sleeping. It's 4 am in my country. When I checked, he has rashes on his thighs, buttocks, and wrists. They can be large or small. He scratches a lot. I gave him 1.5 teaspoons of Tandigyl syrup. Please, doctor, look at his current condition. My husband and I sleep with him on the bed between us. I am 54 years old and had a complete hysterectomy three months ago. Please tell me what this is and what should be done.

My baby is 7 months old. He has foam-like stools, fever, and severe skin issues. Please, doctor, examine this condition. What could be the cause? It started with a severe cold, then he was given paracetamol, cough medicine, and an antibiotic, after which the stools began and were followed by a rash.

You are a doctor, right? I have been applying this Emosone cream to my son, who is an infant (11 months old). For the past 2–3 months, his face and diaper area have developed redness and pimples. I have tried many creams. When he was 6 months old we went to India, and I took him to some doctors there. One of those doctors started him on this Emosone cream, and I have been using it ever since. If I skip the cream for even a day or two, redness and pimples appear on his face, neck, diaper area, and knees, but they clear up again when I resume the cream. I want to know what the actual problem is and how long I need to continue using this cream. Please, doctor, look at his current condition below. If I keep using the cream continuously, could it cause any problems for him now or in the future? Please reply, doctor. Thanks.

My two‑year‑old son has either seborrheic dermatitis or atopic dermatitis, and he also has food allergies—especially to egg protein, dairy, and dry fruits—since March 2014. He experiences severe aggravation from homeopathic medicines, but they do not give good results. He has recurrent rashes all over his body and on his scalp. Please help me, doctor; examine his current condition.

Hi, my 8-year-old son has problems on his hands (including palms) and feet (including soles). He had a few spots last Friday, but today there are many more. He also has pain when swallowing and a large gland under his nose. Please, doctor, examine his current condition. He has also had a mild flu-like illness for a few days. Should I be worried?

My baby boy is 11 months old. For the past three weeks he has been getting a rash (like mosquito bites that start as small dots and then leave black pigment marks, which usually fade within a day). Please, doctor, look at his current condition below. The rash occurs every 2 or 3 days. What could be causing this rash?

My 4‑year‑old daughter has a problem with her skin. Last week she went to the GP because she had a cough, and the doctor thought she might have asthma and a chest infection, so he prescribed amoxicillin, which cleared the cough. A week later (on Thursday) I noticed a rash on her legs that looked like prickly heat, and over a few days it spread over her whole body up to her cheeks. Please, doctor, look at her current condition. She is not feverish, her eyes are bright, there is no obvious fatigue and no itching. It looks a bit like measles or prickly heat. I have given her paracetamol and keep applying calamine cream, but I am worried about what to do. Please help, thank you.

My 18‑month‑old daughter’s vagina looks red instead of pink and she is in some discomfort. There is no diaper rash on the outer skin. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. There are no other symptoms, lumps, or anything extra, but she always tells me that she is in pain. I am worried because I don’t see anything else, just that her vagina is red.

My three-year-old daughter has developed an extensive problem in her vaginal area. It is very red, and there are small spots that look like tiny pustules. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. She has also had a fever since last night. I don’t know if the two are related, but she is now significantly complaining that the area hurts and she does not want anything to touch it. Could this be more than just a common rash?

Hi Doctor, my baby was born very fair, kind of whitish. I am an African woman, and I have a light complexion, and the dad also has a fair complexion. In the first month she developed rashes that gave dark brown dotted coloration between her neck and chest, and that area is still rough, as if something is blending or covering her skin. Please, doctor, look at the current condition. Now her color has become brownish‑fair, but her fingers are still very fair. I don’t know if this is because of the cream I apply to her, which I stop applying on her fingers because she sucks them. The cream is Chicco, and I’ve heard it has both fake and original versions… but please, doctor, is there anything I can eat or do to make my baby’s skin shiny and glowing permanently? I would be grateful for a good result. Thank you, Doctor.

Can a baby have an abnormal growth under a toenail? This growth looks like a deformed nail. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. It now looks like a nail, but it is very difficult to trim, and when it is trimmed a hole forms between the nail and the skin, though there is no bleeding, and it regrows again with the normal nail.

Hello, my daughter is 3 years and 4 months old. Since birth, there has been an odd straight line inside the skin of both of her cheeks. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. We hadn't paid much attention to it before, but now it is more noticeable than before and today she is experiencing a lot of itching. Kindly tell us what we should do. Thank you.

Hello Doctor, my 3‑month‑old baby has very dry skin with red rashes and white patches all over the body. The pediatrician prescribed Atogla cream, which gave good results in the first few days, but after two weeks the skin got as bad as before. We consulted a dermatologist who diagnosed atopic eczema and prescribed Emolene cream. We tried it for a few days, but it had no effect. Which moisturizer is best for eczema that does not contain steroids? Please help my little baby.

My granddaughter's skin is dry, and there are whitish discoloration patches on her legs and hair, and her scalp is also dry. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. We noticed it especially after taking her to the beach. She is only three months old, but it is now becoming more noticeable. Both parents have a history of eczema. What should we do about this; I don't understand...

Hello doctor, my son has some black spots on his scalp crown with a few light scabs that he has scratched off, causing a little bleeding. He doesn't complain of itching, but he is having trouble removing dust from his hair. Should I take him to a physician for a check‑up, or is this just like the dry skin that children sometimes have on their heads? Please examine his current condition and suggest any home remedies. Thank you very much, KA.

My son's neck, just below his right ear, has a swollen red lump. He is in pain and can only move his head a little bit back and forth. Please check what might have happened to his neck down there. He had a CT scan in the ER yesterday, but the swelling wasn't there then, and they were checking for a dislocated shoulder. What should I do? He is only 6 years old and in pain. I am very worried. Could this be an abscess?

My niece went for a check‑up and the doctor noticed that one side of her neck was swollen, so they wanted a scan. The scan showed a problem, and they are now planning to send her to a children's hospital in Dallas. We just want to know what this could be. She will be 13 in August and has high‑functioning autism. Please take a look; something is wrong with her neck.

Yesterday my daughter noticed a small lump on the right side of her jawline, just above the neck. It hurts a lot when touched, and her cheek is slightly swollen. Could this be an infection, a dental problem, or something more serious? Please examine what's happening on her neck.
For the past year, I have had swelling on the right side of my neck. I am 35 years old and a smoker, so I am very stressed. Please examine my current condition.

Since we returned from Nigeria on Thursday, my child has had a problem in the mouth and a high temperature; when she cries, blood comes out from her gums. Please, doctor, examine her mouth. She was given an oral rinse by her GP, which helps with some mouth issues, and she also had a blood test; everything was negative, but blood still comes out of her mouth when she cries. Why? Please help. She is two years old and normally fit and well.

Hi doctor, my 2.5-year-old son had loose motions last month, and it has started again. The stool routine test isn’t showing anything significant, just 1‑2 pus cells per high power field and 1‑2 macrophages per high power field. He also has a mouth ulcer (inside the cheek) that isn’t painful. Please, doctor, look at his mouth. We gave him Gutrite and Gramogyl syrup during the loose motions. Please suggest what to do.

Hello, I currently have a very painful ulcer on the roof of my mouth, which makes eating and drinking very difficult. It is also causing pain in my teeth and the upper line. Please, doctor, examine my mouth below. I am experiencing muscle fatigue even with minimal activity. I am now very tired and feeling a lack of energy, but the most painful symptom is the ulcer on the roof of my mouth. I just want to know what could be causing this and what I should do about it.

Hey doctor, please help. I can't sleep and I'm completely terrified. Seven days ago I smoked a cigarette; I don't smoke much. I only have 5–10 cigarettes occasionally each week. While I was smoking, I felt something in my mouth. Drinking water didn't relieve it, and when I got home I looked in the mirror, opened my mouth, and saw white lesions (ulcers) in my mouth with a white discharge. I cleaned them with cotton. The discharge stopped, but the next day I had two ulcers in my mouth. Please, doctor, examine this condition. On the fourth day there were three, so I consulted an ENT doctor. He examined me and said it was acute tonsillitis. He gave me some antibiotics, but now it’s the eighth day and there’s no improvement in my tonsils. Since the sixth day I’ve had a sore throat, and when I searched my symptoms it shows it could be throat cancer or tonsil cancer. I am really scared; I can’t eat because my mind keeps telling me I will die soon. I keep thinking about my family and feeling that I haven’t done anything good for my parents and society, and now I’m going to die soon. Please, doctor, suggest what is happening to me, whether it’s cancer, and why I can’t sleep because of fear.

My dentist referred me to a pathologist because I have a white ulcer-like lesion on one side of my gums. Is this something I should be worried about like cancer, or could it just be a simple canker sore? I noticed it when I felt a little discomfort, as if there was something between my teeth and cheeks. Please, doctor, look at the lower part of my mouth. I brushed it and irritated the area, causing it to bleed. There's no pain, just a nuisance when I use salt water or mouthwash. I am not a smoker or tobacco user. Please advise. Thank you.

Hi, I think there's a problem with my tooth... In October 2009 I went to a doctor and he told me I should see a dentist because there's an issue with the nerve in my tooth... I don't have money or insurance... The doctor gave me a prescription for Vicodin and penicillin... I took them and everything was fine, but a week ago my tooth started hurting again... In the last 24 hours my face has started swelling, and there's a little swelling under my eye... I don't understand what's happening... Please give me any advice. Can you answer my health questions now? For the procedure, look at my mouth below. Please write your query here.

My 3‑year‑old son has a small red flat dot on his upper lip. There’s no drainage or swelling and the size stays the same (like a pinprick). It won’t go away. I’ve tried OTC cortisone and Neosporin. Please, doctor, look at this current condition. When I apply Vaseline it looks a little better but it never completely disappears. It’s a perfect circle and flat. He recently took antibiotics for an infection and the dot remained unchanged. He isn’t bothered by it, but my pediatrician and I don’t know what it is. He has no significant medical history. I’m looking for a pediatric dermatologist in my area. My pediatrician thinks it’s not a concern. My son’s skin is sensitive and he has a history of eczema—the last flare was two years ago. He constantly wipes and rubs his mouth.

My 5-year-old child had a low fever since morning, which became high by evening. I gave him baby Tylenol and his fever dropped to 99. At night he woke up hungry, with a good appetite, but his eyes, cheeks, and lips were swollen. Please, doctor, look at his current condition. Later his eyes seemed a bit better (not completely), but his upper lip is still swelling. Please advise.

My son was diagnosed with strep throat on Thursday. He was prescribed amoxicillin (to be given twice daily) and was told to continue alternating Tylenol and ibuprofen. I am following the directions, and today he is complaining of mouth pain, and when he went to brush his teeth his gums were bleeding. His gums are also swollen, and his lips are starting to swell. Please, doctor, look at his current condition below. Are these symptoms due to the strep, or is he having an allergic reaction to the medication? His father is allergic to amoxicillin.

My daughter has had severe swelling in her lips and some other areas for the past six days. Please, doctor, examine her current condition. There is light blistering and redness on the outer part of her lips. We went to the emergency department, and the doctors thought it might be related to an allergy, but Benadryl and Reactine only work occasionally.

I don't exactly know what my question is, but for a long time I've had a swollen neck, tightness in my neck, swollen lips, and my jawbones are becoming visible; my whole body feels tense and I look strange from the outside. Please, doctor, examine this current condition.

I have some problems in my mouth. The inside of my lower lip is swollen and painful, and there's a small swelling on my upper lip that burns. Lately it's getting better, but my front gums are swollen and hurt when I brush. I had my teeth cleaned fairly recently; I go every six months. Please, doctor, look at my current condition. This is new—I started using an all‑natural powder instead of toothpaste, but I stopped it yesterday. I don’t remember when I was last sick. It feels like it might be viral, and I’m not sure what’s happening. Thanks a lot!

My son is 12 years old. He has had knee pain for four months. The pain is under the kneecap. I have taken him to the doctor five times for the pain. He has not had any X-ray or test yet. Please, doctor, look at his current condition below. They keep saying it is a sports injury and will get better with time. He started limping last week, and there is a lump and swelling under the kneecap. I am very worried now. Can you tell me if this is something else or just a sports injury.

My son, who is about three to four years old, woke up crying yesterday morning and complained of pain in his left leg. Since then he has refused to stand or walk. There is no visible swelling, redness, or bruising. Please, doctor, examine his current condition. He moves around on the bed or sofa, but any pressure on the leg causes him pain, and bending it also hurts; with assistance and encouragement he can be made to move again. He has an appointment today for a check‑up, but we would like additional advice. Thank you.

My 13-year-old daughter sprained her knee while playing tackleball during the first week of June. An orthopedic doctor ordered an MRI, which came back clear. About a month and a half later, when she started playing soccer, her condition got worse instead of improving, so she is now seeing a physical therapist. She sees the therapist once every two weeks for 6–8 weeks. She is worried because, despite strength stretches, ice, and ibuprofen, she is not getting better. She is back on crutches and wearing a full leg brace to keep the knee from moving. Her knee is swollen and she feels pain under the knee in a horseshoe shape. Please, doctor, evaluate this current condition. I don’t understand what the next step should be.

My 10-year-old son has a sudden onset of eye swelling, with pain radiating down to his knees. Sometimes the swelling is so severe that it cannot be touched. Please, doctor, examine this current condition. There has been no injury. It has been ongoing for about three weeks. Touching it causes pain, and he complains of shooting, stabbing pain from his foot to his knee.

Hello, my 6-year-old son woke up with a severe headache, moderate to high fever, red eyes, and he is crying. Please, doctor, look at his eyes. I gave him children's Advil and now I'm wondering if I should do anything else, and when I should take him to his pediatrician. He never gets sick; in fact, this is the first time he's been ill since school started in September.

Hello Doctor, my one-year-old daughter has had redness in her left eye for a week. We consulted a pediatric specialist, and they said she should receive Ceplox eye drops every hour for a day. However, it hasn't improved yet. Could you give your valuable opinion?

My 8-year-old son has allergies. He has heavy redness under both eyes and between the bridge of his nose. His skin looks as if blood has been spilled in the red areas. Please, doctor, look at the eyes in the lower image. His skin is a bright red, like a sunburn color. He says he only occasionally feels itching now. The rest of his face is a normal color. Please give advice.

My 4‑year‑old child's eyes turned red after going to the swimming pool last Friday. Please look at the lower part of the eyes. No one reported any itching or pain. The redness lasted for 2–3 days and then gradually faded. He went back to the pool yesterday and his eyes are red again. There is no itching or pain. Should I be concerned?

Hello, I have a three-year-old son whom I took to the ER two days ago. I thought he had pink eye, and they gave me an antibiotic cream for his eyes. However, his eyes are still red and gooey, and he has a very strange nose and cough. Should I take him to my regular doctor tomorrow morning? Please, doctor, look at his eyes below. There are also two other boys and myself at home, and even though pink eye is highly infectious, none of us have gotten it. Could he have been misdiagnosed?

Hello doctor, my son is four years old... for the past year he has had a habit of snoring when he sleeps at night... when he has a cold or cough, the sound gets louder... we consider it normal and ignore it. Recently we planned a minor surgery for his phimosis. When the doctor gave anesthesia, he developed bronchospasm and acute laryngeal issues. Please doctor, look at his current condition. Then the doctor called us for further check‑up to find the cause. They observed that he breathes through his nose at night. Then the doctor suggested a digital X‑ray of the upper airways, which showed mild enlargement of the adenoid gland (type 2). However, our doctor still suspects a problem with his larynx. He advised us to see an ENT specialist. Honestly, we are completely worried. We do not know the exact cause of our child's adverse reaction to anesthesia. The doctor hinted that he may need surgery.

I have a four‑year‑old son who has a lump on the back of his hand that has been there since the weekend; it feels hard when pressed but I can squeeze it, there is no pain on touch, and there is no history of injury or a splinter. No bone or nerve appears to be involved nearby. Please, doctor, examine this current condition.

My 2‑month‑old baby has long, thick hair. She pulls her hair a lot (since day 1). When she’s hungry or trying to soothe herself, she starts sucking her hand or thumb. I thought about applying petroleum jelly to her hair so her hair and scalp don’t get damaged or dry, but I’m wondering what negative effects continuous use of petroleum jelly might have. Please, doctor, look at this carefully.

My son woke up this morning and his neck is very swollen. The swelling has changed the appearance of his neck. His normally round eyes now have an "Eurasian" look, and his face has taken on a "Mongoloid" appearance. His lips are also very swollen—as if a mouse bit them. Last night he was given some cough syrup for the kids, and he ate toast, cheese, and used mustard. He has no known allergies. He says he feels "fine" and has no pain in his ears, throat, mouth, eyes, or nose. Should we take him to a doctor? Please see the image of the affected area below, doctor.

I have a two-and-a-half-year-old son who is still in diapers, and small red pimples are appearing on the skin around his penis. Is this due to irritation from his urine, or should I be more concerned? Please see the image below showing the affected area.

Doctor, my 9-year-old son has been suffering from headaches for two days, and I have some problem with my eyes. Please look at the image of the affected area below. My daughter is 6.5 years old, 38 pounds, 42 inches tall. She has a small boil‑like red growth on her skin; I think it might be a clitoris, but I'm not sure. Please see the image below. Sometimes it hurts, especially when it contacts a pillow or cushion. She also feels discomfort at school when she sits cross‑legged, and after urinating she experiences itching or a crawling sensation in that area. Should we have an urologist or pediatrician check it, or will it heal on its own? Please help.

My baby is five months old. I noticed today that there is a rash under the skin on his head. I'm wondering if I should be concerned about this. I handle him carefully. My 3‑year‑old son still wears diapers at night. Suddenly, a red group of bumps has appeared on the skin above his hand and between his toes, and he is scratching them. Could this possibly be a diaper rash or something serious that needs attention? Please see the image of the affected area below.
